A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PrivTune, PrivBench, and privacy-tuning research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite restructuring and some inconsistent reported values.

before.justification: v3 reports original benchmark evaluations, privacy-tuning experiments, data-efficiency and generalization analyses, and a five-reviewer study of dataset labels.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results and adds InternVL2.5 evaluations, prompt-sensitivity experiments, and expanded benchmark-size analysis.

M1.justification: The proposed Privacy VLM family expands from TinyLLaVA to include InternVL2.5-2B and 4B, using different language and vision backbones. This is a limited model extension: the PrivTune dialogue-generation process and LoRA privacy-tuning approach remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation retain PrivTune, PrivBench, PrivBench-H, VISPR, PrivacyAlert, Biv-Priv, VQAv2, POPE, ScienceQA, and Places365. The same four languages and held-out privacy categories remain covered. Additional model configurations and prompt wordings do not introduce new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: InternVL2.5-2B and 4B are added as untuned comparators in the privacy benchmarks. The benchmark-size comparison replaces CoAgent in v3 Table 6 with LLaVA in v4 Figure 7. BLIP/InstructBLIP is a relabeling of the retained result series, not an additional comparator.

E3.justification: v4 introduces per-model selection among four prompts using PrivTune, separate from evaluation data; privacy-tuned models and GPT-4 use fixed P1. This substantively revises the baseline evaluation protocol. Benchmark-size testing expands from random 50% subsets to 20–90% fractions, and its tuned model changes from TinyLLaVA to InternVL-4B. Existing TinyLLaVA training budgets and human-study settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix C systematically tests sensitivity to four prompt wordings across baselines and privacy-tuned models. Figure 7 substantially extends the benchmark-size robustness analysis beyond v3's single sampling fraction. The Discussion also newly reports unsuccessful in-context-learning and chain-of-thought trials, without quantitative details. Leave-one-class-out tests, training-data sensitivity, and dataset-label audits were already present.

E5.justification: Table 12 newly reports means and standard deviations across prompt variants. Benchmark subsampling retains 100 repetitions, but v4 presents standard-deviation curves instead of v3's mean-and-standard-deviation table. Neither PDF establishes an increase in repeated training runs or seeds.

E6.justification: Main and appendix results are extensively revised and expanded. For example, Table 2 changes Otter's PrivBench MCC from -0.87 to 0.29 under the revised prompt protocol; this is not a same-setting improvement. Tuned TinyLLaVA remains at 0.86, while newly evaluated tuned InternVL-4B reports 0.90. New prompt and subsampling results are added. Some v4 entries disagree across tables, including tuned InternVL-2B results.

T1.justification: The binary privacy formulation, conditional dialogue-generation expression, and MCC definition are retained. The privacy-rate formula newly displayed in the main text already appeared in v3 Appendix J. No substantive mathematical definitions, assumptions, proofs, or derivations are added.

C1.justification: The abstract expands the evaluated population from ten to twelve VLMs and changes from one Privacy VLM tuned on 100 samples to multiple variants tuned on a few hundred samples. The 100-sample finding remains for TinyLLaVA. The central claims about dataset quality and data-efficient privacy tuning persist.

C2.justification: v4 newly acknowledges possible pretraining contamination from Re-LAION images, explains why per-class InternVL-4B MCC can trail aggregate MCC, and distinguishes visual-detection failures from failures to recognize privacy. It also qualifies image–text misalignment as potential and gives training-data differences as an explicit alternative explanation for language effects.

D1.justification: v4 adds exact evaluation prompts, selection rules, backbone information, and InternVL tuning settings; it also discloses cosine scheduling and a 0.03 warmup ratio. A concrete repository link replaces the earlier promised page. Dataset distribution changes from an encrypted dataset under Apache 2.0 to requested URLs and annotations, with labels, splits, and dialogues under CC BY-NC 4.0 and explicit redistribution restrictions.

R1.justification: v4 adds the InternVL-related Chen et al. reference and removes Hong et al.'s CogAgent reference, although CoAgent remains evaluated. It modestly refines the distinction between privacy understanding and sensitive-attribute inference. Most other bibliography changes update publication details rather than add research.

P1.justification: v4 shortens the title, updates affiliations, edits wording and spelling, reorders contributions, and moves dataset motivation from Appendix A into Section 4. It removes the separate supplementary cover and contents page and inserts a prompts appendix. Most existing prose and the overall section sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The journal-style reformatting substantially changes typography, table widths, and placement. Tables 2, 3, and 5 gain structure and model rows; v3 Table 6 becomes v4 Figure 7. v4 adds three prompt tables and two negative-example grids. Its main-text Table 8 redisplays three existing appendix analyses rather than introducing new findings.

improvement.justification: Prompt-selection controls, cross-backbone validation, and explicit prompts/settings strengthen the central empirical argument and reproducibility relative to v3. These benefits support a limited net improvement, but reporting inconsistencies constrain confidence in exact results: tuned InternVL-2B's PrivBench-H MCC is 0.36 in Table 2 versus 0.53 in Table 15, and Otter's VISPR MCC has opposite signs in Tables 2 and 16. The claim that all Privacy VLMs outperform the comparators also exceeds what Table 2 establishes.
